validity.researcher_notes: gem.wiki page 403'd (Cloudflare) on direct fetch, consistent with the scope note that the harvest failed tracker-wide; the sheet's own [ref] cells for this row are ALL MISSING_REF (Status/Fuel/PipelineType/Length/Diameter/Location/Owner) -- so there is no existing citation to re-verify, and per the scope guidance a row with zero cited support and zero independently found support is a legitimate existence flag, not a non-finding. I ran the exact pipeline name ('Faisalabad-Shahdara' + 'gas pipeline', both word orders, with and without SNGPL/OGRA qualifiers) through Bing, Google, DuckDuckGo (html + lite), Ecosia, Mojeek, Marginalia, Brave, and Yahoo via WebFetch (WebSearch tool itself was already at its session budget cap before I could use it). None returned a page that specifically names a 'Faisalabad-Shahdara' gas pipeline; most returned unrelated/junk results (lottery pages, speedtest.net, tourism pages) or were blocked (403/429) or CAPTCHA-gated (DDG). archive.org/web.archive.org is not fetchable from this environment either, so I could not check an older cached copy of the wiki page for its original footnotes. SNGPL's own site (sngpl.com.pk) has only a navigational 'Transmission System' stub page with no segment-level content reachable without a working site search. One Urdu-script query (فیصل آباد / شاہدرہ گیس پائپ لائن) via Bing also returned nothing relevant. What I DID find, independently: (1) Wikipedia's SNGPL article (verified live, 200, contains 'Faisalabad') states 'the main transmission regions of SNGPL are Faisalabad, Lahore, Multan, and Wah' and that SNGPL's max transmission diameter is ~42in -- both consistent with, but not specific confirmation of, this row (16in dia, Faisalabad origin, SNGPL 100% owner all fit the general pattern). (2) A DuckDuckGo-lite result surfaced a personal blog listing a 'Shahdara Sub Region' SNGPL office address -- too weak/unreliable to cite as a ref, but it corroborates that Shahdara is a real SNGPL operational node, consistent with Shahdara also appearing as an endpoint in the separately-rostered P4139 (Shahdara-Gujranwala-Rahwali Gas Pipeline), so 'Shahdara' itself is not an invented place in this dataset. Geographically the ~119 km figure is plausible for a Faisalabad-to-Lahore-area corridor (road distance is roughly 130-140 km). None of this, however, rises to an independent source that specifically names THIS pipeline or confirms its length/diameter -- it is plausibility, not confirmation. Classification (transmission, Gas, SNGPL 100% owner) is internally consistent with the roster's dozens of similarly-named, similarly-specified Punjab SNGPL trunk/loop segments (P4133-P4182), which read as a single bulk table load (all LastUpdated 2023-07-07/10/11) -- most plausibly derived from an OGRA or SNGPL network-inventory document neither of which is crawlable via general search from this environment. No duplicate match found on the roster: P4136 (Faisalabad-Shahdara Gas Pipeline-II, 112.51 km) is a distinct but geographically/thematically paired 'I/II' loopline, matching the same I/II/III augmentation pattern seen elsewhere in this roster (Sui-Multan Loopline I/II/III, Wah-Nowshera I/II, Dandot-Gali Jagir-Wah I/II) -- this looks like a legitimate original-line-plus-augmentation pair, not a double-count of one physical pipe under two ProjectIDs, though I could not independently confirm either line's existence to be fully certain. Net: I cannot rule out that this is a real SNGPL segment correctly transcribed from a primary network inventory, but I also cannot independently confirm it given the tools available this pass -- flagging as a low-tier existence concern per the scope instruction rather than silently passing it.
